items.name: 〜です
items.summary: です follows a noun or na-adjective to state politely what something is (X is Y). It is the polite form learners produce first; the plain equivalent is だ.

items.name: 〜か
items.summary: The particle か at the end of a sentence turns a statement into a question, without changing word order.

items.name: 〜ます
items.summary: The ます-form is the polite non-past form of a verb, used for present and future affirmative actions.

items.name: 〜ません
items.summary: ません is the polite negative of a verb (does not / will not do). Its past is ませんでした.

items.name: 〜じゃありません
items.summary: じゃありません (more formal: ではありません) is the polite negative of です — it states that something is not the case.

items.name: あります・います
items.summary: あります expresses the existence of inanimate things; います is used for people and animals. The thing that exists is marked with が.

items.name: 〜が好きです
items.summary: The na-adjective 好き, with its object marked by が, expresses what someone likes; 嫌い (dislike) works the same way.

items.name: 〜ましょう

items.name: 〜から
items.summary: から follows a clause to give a reason or cause (because …, so …). The reason comes first, the result after.

items.summary: The て-form of a verb followed by いる (polite います) expresses an action in progress or a resulting, continuing state.

items.name: 〜くなる・〜になる
items.summary: なる expresses a change of state. い-adjectives drop い and take く, na-adjectives and nouns take に, before なる.
